## 1. A mosque built for harm  (`#a-mosque-built-for-harm`)

Cited ayat: 9:107-110

> **9:107** وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ مَسْجِدًا ضِرَارًا وَكُفْرًا وَتَفْرِيقًۢا بَيْنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَإِرْصَادًا لِّمَنْ حَارَبَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنَآ إِلَّا ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
>
> **9:108** لَا تَقُمْ فِيهِ أَبَدًا لَّمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ أَن تَقُومَ فِيهِ فِيهِ رِجَالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَن يَتَطَهَّرُوا۟ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُطَّهِّرِينَ
>
> **9:109** أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ تَقْوَىٰ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضْوَٰنٍ خَيْرٌ أَم مَّنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ فَٱنْهَارَ بِهِۦ فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
>
> **9:110** لَا يَزَالُ بُنْيَٰنُهُمُ ٱلَّذِى بَنَوْا۟ رِيبَةً فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلَّآ أَن تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (9:107): There are those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of lying in wait for one who had fought God and His messenger before.

**c2** (9:107): They will swear that they wanted only the best, and God bears witness that they are liars.

**c3** (9:108): The one addressed is told never to stand in it.

**c4** (9:108): A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy of his standing in it; in it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.

**c5** (9:109): The verse asks whether one who founded his building on fear of God and His approval is better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, which collapsed with him into the fire of Hell; God does not guide the wrongdoing people.

**c6** (9:110): The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts, until their hearts are cut into pieces; God is knowing and wise.

### One-minute summary

The verses speak of those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief and for dividing the believers [c1]. They say that God bears witness that these people are liars when they swear that they wanted only the best [c2]. The one addressed is told never to stand in it [c3], and the verses speak of a mosque founded on piety from the first day [c4].

### Complete story

There are those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of lying in wait for one who had fought God and His messenger before [c1]. They will swear that they wanted only the best, and God bears witness that they are liars [c2].

The one addressed is told never to stand in it [c3]. A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy of his standing in it; in it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves [c4].

The verse asks whether one who founded his building on fear of God and His approval is better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, which collapsed with him into the fire of Hell; God does not guide the wrongdoing people [c5]. The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts, until their hearts are cut into pieces; God is knowing and wise [c6].

### Deep study

The passage names the purposes of those who built it: harm, disbelief, division and lying in wait [c1]. It reports what they will swear and God's witness against it [c2]. It then sets buildings side by side, one founded on piety and one on the edge of a crumbling bank [c4][c5]. It does not name the builders, the place, or the one they lay in wait for [c1].

### Kids mode

The verses speak of people who took a mosque for harm and to divide the believers [c1]. They say that a mosque founded on piety is more worthy [c4]. They say that in it are men who love to purify themselves, and that God loves those who purify themselves [c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage judges a building by what it was founded on: piety and God's approval on one side, harm and division on the other [c1][c5]. Another is that it speaks of purifying oneself as something God loves [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: where the mosque stood, who built it, when, or what became of it. The verses give none of this.
- Not established: who 'one who had fought God and His messenger before' is.
- Not established: which mosque is 'founded on piety from the first day', or who the men are who love to purify themselves.
- Not established: whether 'stand in it' refers to prayer; the verse says only 'stand'.
- Not established: what the 'doubt in their hearts' refers to beyond the words of 9:110.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the builders, the place, the occasion and what followed. None is used in the story texts.
